title: Context-dependent determinants of CRISPR-Cas9 editing efficiency revealed through cross-species endogenous editing analysis
abstract: Accurate prediction of CRISPR-Cas9 guide RNA (gRNA) editing efficiency remains limited, particularly outside human systems, where models trained on exogenous human datasets show poor generalization. We analyzed Cas9 efficiency and repair outcomes using novel endogenous editing data from four human cell types, two tomato cell types, and cells from giant river prawn and black soldier fly. While integrating publicly available predictors via ensemble frameworks improved performance, our analysis revealed hundreds of novel features affecting activity. Crucially, dominant features related to sites' competition for gRNA, and local geometric properties varied across systems, highlighting the strong context dependence of Cas9 efficiency and arguing against a universal model. Interestingly, codon usage bias-based features also emerged as informative predictors, as they are proxies for chromatin accessibility. In contrast, trends in repair outcomes remained conserved. This work provides essential resources for more generalizable CRISPR guide design.
cell_systems: human PLX placenta-derived mesenchymal-like adherent stromal cells
Macrobrachium rosenbergii (giant river prawn) embryonic cells
relevance: The strongest direct argument for cell-context-aware guide scoring: with endogenous RNP editing at 1005 sites across 8 cell systems (including BOTH primary human T cells and K562), sequence-only public predictors collapse (DeepCRISPR 0.96 Spearman on its own data -> 0.08 on these human endogenous data; SPROUT 0.41 -> 0.11), and the dominant efficiency features flip sign between cell types (e.g. local PAM-adjacent site density is negative in K562 but positive in U937 and tomato). It supplies a concrete 557-feature engineering catalogue including an explicit epigenetics/accessibility family (DNase-seq accessibility, CTCF, H3K4me3, DNA methylation motifs, Hi-C/TADbit 3D density), DNA-shape (MGW, Roll, HelT, ProT), gRNA thermodynamics/scaffold folding, codon-usage-bias proxies for accessibility, and off-target competition counts - plus the recommendation to make competition/off-target metrics chromatin-aware.
